title: ISS TEPC dose and dose equivalent, 1 minute, 3 to 16 September 2017
documentation: https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/misc/NotesI.html#ISS_DOSANL_TEPC ('Experiment Data, ISS TEPC (from ASCII DOS.TXT file), Edward Semones (NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group/Johnson Space Center)')
https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/iss-tissue-equivalent-proportional-counter-tepc-dose-analyzer-10-s-data-61b24 (NASA Open Data Portal record; license https://www.usa.gov/government-works)
instrument: ISS Tissue Equivalent Proportional Counter (TEPC), NASA Space Radiation Analysis Group, CDAWeb dataset ISS_DOSANL_TEPC (coverage 2010-04-29 to 2018-04-11). The data.nasa.gov record describes the JAXA PS-TEPC; the CDAWeb notes name the NASA SRAG TEPC, which this file follows. Module location is not given in the dataset.

column 4 (TIME_INTERVAL).description: Minutes over which the data was collected

preprocessing: None; the HAPI CSV response saved as supplied. HAPI CSV has no header row: the column names and units above come from the HAPI info response. Fill value is -1.0E31; this window has none.
license: US Government work (https://www.usa.gov/government-works, per the NASA Open Data Portal record). US Government work. Credit NASA as the source; no NASA logo or insignia is used (NASA-SOURCES.md section 4).
provenance_note: REPLAY of recorded NASA CDAWeb data, shown with its 2017 UTC timestamps.
is_not: An area instrument's dose and dose equivalent at one location, not a crew member's personal dose or effective dose (NASA career limits use effective dose).
Rates per minute, not per hour: convert with the unit, never by assumption.

consumers.use: Second, independent instrument for the same event, with dose equivalent in uSv and explicit UTC; lets the feed carry both uGy and uSv with their UCUM units. Gives the upper end of the peak hourly factor for the station_solar_particle_event scenario (about 19x at the TEPC versus about 7x at DosTel2).

consumers.component: radiation warning rules and mission dose tally
consumers.use: Golden input for the running dose tally: each rate times its TIME_INTERVAL, summed over a UTC day, gives about 410 uGy (about 900 uSv) on quiet days and about 830 uGy (about 1,710 uSv) on 11 September (README).
A real daily series (dose per day) with one outlier day for testing the deterministic trend and the forecast evaluation on non-personal data; never a personal indicator.
Data for the cases/spe-2017-09-iss-columbus known-outcome case.

notes: Hourly profile computed the same way (readings outside latitude -55 to 5 and longitude -95 to 20, DOSE times 60 for uGy/h, divided by the median hourly mean of 3 to 9 September, 5.64 uGy/h): peak hours on 11 September at 09:00 UTC (106.8 uGy/h, 18.9x), 07:00 (17.6x), 10:00 (14.8x) and 05:00 (12.9x); 7.3x to 7.6x at 08:00, 11:00 and 12:00. The TEPC (location not given) reads a higher peak factor than DosTel2 in Columbus, so a simulator should cite the instrument it takes the factor from.
